questions.question: Why should AI Ecosystem and Vendor Landscape be taught as a workflow instead of only as tool awareness?
options: Because the vendor with the most impressive demo is usually the right choice for the stack
Because a copilot and a vector database can be compared as direct alternatives to each other
Because teams need shared signals, controls, and decision rules they can apply to real work
Because brand familiarity is a reliable shortcut when a team lacks a map of the ecosystem
questions.explanation: The lesson is built around reusable operating artifacts — shared signals, controls, and decision rules — not the idea that the best demo wins, that a copilot and a vector database are alternatives, or that brand familiarity substitutes for an ecosystem map.

questions.question: In the lesson's opening example, why did the vendor discussion turn brand-driven?
options: Every shortlisted vendor refused to run a pilot test before a contract was signed, leaving no evidence, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases
The evaluation criteria were drawn so narrowly that only a single supplier could ever satisfy them
Data residency requirements ruled out every vendor the team was most interested in evaluating first
The team had no shared map of the AI stack, so tools from different layers were compared as alternatives
questions.explanation: The lesson's opening example has a team comparing a copilot, an agent platform, a vector database, and a workflow tool as if they were alternatives; without a shared map of the layered ecosystem the conversation defaults to brands — not because of a pilot refusal, over-narrow criteria, or a data residency exclusion.

questions.question: What does the Python artifact produce for AI Ecosystem and Vendor Landscape?
options: A signed vendor contract ready for procurement to countersign
A ranked plan with category, score, priority, controls, and rationale
A live feature comparison scraped from each vendor's own website, because one plausible output is sufficient production evidence
A single winner per category, chosen without stated criteria
questions.explanation: The lesson's Python artifact outputs a ranked plan — category, score, priority, controls, and rationale — not a procurement-ready contract, a scraped feature comparison, or an unexplained per-category winner.

questions.question: Which control belongs to the lesson design?
options: Letting a polished vendor demo stand in for the pilot test the team still owes itself
Skipping the security review because the vendor is already used elsewhere in the group
Evaluation criteria, written down before demos so the comparison rests on evidence not hype
Postponing the exit plan until lock-in risk has already shown up in a renewal negotiation, before defining the measurement, acceptance threshold, or rollback path
questions.explanation: The lesson's controls include evaluation criteria defined before demos, keeping the decision on evidence instead of hype — the opposite of treating a demo as a pilot, skipping the security review, or postponing the exit plan until lock-in bites.

questions.question: When should a scenario become a launch-gate discussion rather than a casual awareness exercise?
options: Only when the vendor's product happens to be hosted outside the European Union
Only when a vendor demo has revealed a feature that the architecture review did not anticipate
When impact, uncertainty, and matched risk signals such as lock-in risk are all running high
Never — a vendor choice can always be revisited at the next contract renewal window
questions.explanation: High-impact, uncertain, lock-in-heavy vendor decisions need a launch gate regardless of hosting location, what a demo happened to surface, or whether a renewal window is coming.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the output template?
options: To formally replace procurement's authority over which vendor finally gets signed
To keep the known weaknesses of the preferred vendor out of the comparison entirely
To automatically generate completion certificates for participants once the workshop ends
To create a reusable matrix or prompt that teams can keep applying after the course ends
questions.explanation: The output template is an ecosystem map and vendor evaluation matrix teams keep applying after the course — not a substitute for procurement authority, a way to hide a favored vendor's weaknesses, or an automatic certificate generator.
